dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I don't believe anyone enjoys taking up arms and going to war unless they're seeking to fulfill some other desire.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Whenever the sound of clashing blades fades into the distance, I appreciate the silence that follows all the more.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Too quiet for you? Then I'll play a tune on the leaf, so you can be surrounded with the sound of nature.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: There are many reasons why a samurai might draw their blade, but the principle is always the same: To do what they know in their heart is right.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Though we walk a perilous path, where powerful foes face us at every turn, and though I cannot sense what lies at its end, I tread onwards with no fear in my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: My mind is at ease, for I tread this path in your company.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: During my days as a wanderer, if I came upon a beautiful view and was feeling in a poetic mood, I'd stop to compose a few lines.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I once thought about writing an anthology of my poems and leaving it on a shelf, so I could share with others the way I felt when my eyes first met those wonderful sights.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: But when I looked back at the drivel I'd written, I gave up on the idea. I'm sure other travelers will get that same sense of peace from the natural world as I did, if it's meant to be.
